name: Architecture Conformance
target_flow: HTTP -> Application -> Domain -> Contracts -> Infrastructure -> Persistence/External
method: Every class under app/ was parsed for use statements and grouped by layer, then each cross-layer edge was inspected for its actual purpose. Facade and SDK usage was grepped per layer. No dependency was classified as a violation without reading what it is used for.

findings.dependency: App\Services\LoyaltyService, SettingsService, PricingRuleEngine, Pricing\{ScreenPricingResolver, DailyPricingCalculator, ReferralPricingCalculator, FirstBookingDiscountPricingCalculator} (7 imports)
findings.rule: Rule 2 (pure domain invariants) + Rule 11 (strict layer dependency direction): Domain must not depend on a concrete Infrastructure or legacy service layer
findings.evidence: Parsed from the file's use statements. The engine needs loyalty point-value conversion, DB-backed settings and five stateless calculators.
findings.action: Deferred to Phase 0.15. Correct end state is value-object parameters on the calculators plus a PricingSettingsProvider contract; that is a financial-determinism change requiring its own approved phase.

findings.rule: Domain should not depend on Active Record models
findings.evidence: The stateless pricing calculators accept Eloquent models as parameters, so relocating them to Domain would relocate the leak rather than remove it.
findings.action: Deferred together with the 7 service imports above; same root cause.

findings.rule: Domain value object should not reference the persistence model
findings.evidence: Inspecting the file: the status vocabulary is defined over Payment constants.
findings.action: Deferred: the status vocabulary is genuinely Payment-domain knowledge, but the reference direction should be inverted (Payment -> PaymentStatus, not PaymentStatus -> Payment).

findings.rule: A repository contract may name its aggregate
findings.evidence: Architecture Rule 6 permits repository boundaries where persistence isolation is justified. Naming the aggregate in a repository contract is intentional and does not leak persistence implementation.
findings.action: None. This is the designed pattern.

findings.action: None. This is the designed pattern.

findings.dependency: No App\Http, no Http::, no Mail::, no Storage::, no Guzzle, no Razorpay SDK
findings.rule: Domain must not depend on HTTP or external SDKs
findings.evidence: grep -rnE 'App\\Http|Http::|Mail::|Storage::|Guzzle|Razorpay' app/Domain/ returned no matches.

findings.dependency: No app() or resolve() service locator
findings.rule: Domain must not use the service locator
findings.evidence: grep -rnE '[^>a-zA-Z_$](app|resolve)\(' app/Domain returned no matches (the only apparent hits were ReportPeriod::resolve in Application).

findings.rule: Application may orchestrate legacy services during the strangler migration
findings.evidence: Every use case and reporting query that still depends on App\Services was enumerated. This is the expected transitional state under Architecture Rule 7: wrap and delegate first, extract deeper domain behaviour later.
findings.action: Tracked as debt. The Application -> Services edges are the concrete work list for future extraction phases.

findings.rule: Application must not depend on the HTTP layer
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'App\\Http' app/Application/ returned no matches.

findings.dependency: No Http::, Mail::, Storage::, Guzzle, Razorpay
findings.rule: Application must not call external facades or SDKs directly
findings.evidence: grep -rnE 'Http::|Mail::|Storage::|Guzzle|Razorpay' app/Application/ returned no matches. External access is behind Infrastructure contracts.

findings.rule: Application owns the transaction boundary
findings.evidence: The use case owns the campaign-booking transaction; the controller no longer contains DB::transaction for that flow.

findings.dependency: Eloquent, Razorpay SDK, Google OAuth, HTTP client, Mail facade, Storage facade, GD
findings.rule: Infrastructure is the only layer permitted to know vendor and framework I/O
findings.evidence: All Razorpay, Google, exchange-rate, mail, storage and GD usage is confined here. Verified by grep: the only Mail:: call site in app/ is LaravelMailAdapter; the only GD call sites are GdImageProcessor.

findings.rule: Facade must be confined to the adapter
findings.evidence: grep -rnE '[^a-zA-Z_]Mail::(to|send|queue|raw|html)' app/ matched only this file.

findings.rule: HTTP should delegate storage to the application/port layer
findings.evidence: AuthorController (2), SuccessStoryController (2), GalleryController (2), ScreenController (1), ScreenProviderPortalController (1), JobApplicationController (1). Left in place by explicit user decision in Phase 0.12 to avoid touching unrelated features.
findings.action: Tracked as debt; the first integration item recommended for the next phase.

findings.rule: A model must not depend on the HTTP layer
findings.evidence: RESOLVED in Phase 0.13. User::hasPermission() now resolves app/Support/Authorization/RolePermissionChecker. Verified: no App\Http import remains in any model.

findings.rule: Middleware should be a thin HTTP adapter over the authorization boundary
findings.evidence: The middleware now injects RolePermissionChecker and delegates both userHasPermission and clearPermissionCache to it; the permission algorithm no longer lives in the transport layer.

findings.rule: HTTP must not talk to external SDKs (Architecture Rule 1)
findings.evidence: No SDK or Http:: usage. Payment operations are reached through Application use cases.

findings.rule: Controllers should be thin HTTP adapters
findings.evidence: Reduced from 1827 to 1414 lines in Phase 0.13 by extracting storeCampaign (299->50), update (130->15) and checkConflicts (84->19). Remaining methods are predominantly single-purpose reads and simple state transitions.
findings.action: Continue: the approval/media-review/session methods are the next extraction candidates.

findings.rule: Reporting must perform no writes and no business-rule decisions
findings.evidence: Zero write calls (create/update/delete/insert) under app/Application/Reporting. Reporting reads persisted revenue splits and the partner_commissions ledger rather than recomputing them.

findings.rule: Reporting should not depend on transactional services
findings.evidence: Some queries read SettingsService for thresholds and a couple reference ReportService symbols. Read-only, so no mutation risk, but it is a residual coupling.

findings.dependency: app(LoyaltyService, SettingsService, ReferralTrackingService) x7 in updated/deleting model events and getLoyaltySummary()
findings.rule: A persistence model should not drive cross-domain financial side effects
findings.evidence: Model events reverse loyalty points and cancel/refund referral tracking on every status transition, resolved through the service locator because model events cannot be injected.
findings.action: Deferred to Phase 0.15 as the highest-priority item. The side effects are correct and covered; extracting them changes when they commit, which is a financial-semantics change.

findings.dependency: Static::booted() global scope and status hooks
findings.rule: Business rules should not live in model events
findings.evidence: A global scope excludes payment_pending bookings from default queries, and status hooks drive loyalty/referral.
findings.action: Documented; the global scope is load-bearing for reporting and booking queries.
